topics: Big-O describes how time or memory grows with input size: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).
A block of contiguous memory with O(1) index access; insertion or deletion in the middle costs O(n).
Nodes holding data plus a pointer to the next node. Fast insert/delete, slow random access.
LIFO structure: push and pop at the top. Used in undo, recursion and expression evaluation.
FIFO structure: enqueue at the rear, dequeue at the front. Used in scheduling and BFS.
Hierarchical nodes. A binary search tree keeps left < root < right, giving O(log n) search when balanced.
Vertices connected by edges. Traversed with BFS (queue) or DFS (stack/recursion).
Bubble, selection and insertion sort are O(n²); merge and quick sort are O(n log n) on average.
Linear search is O(n); binary search needs sorted data and runs in O(log n).
